newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down on late dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down on late dlr demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened on dollar demand to end Tuesday at 35.83/84 per dollar against the day's opening quotes of 35.81/82, dealers said.
They said the rupee traded at a high of 35.81 and a low of 35.84 against the dollar in dull trade on Tuesday.

"Trade was basically quiet today. The rupee moved up soon after business commenced on lack of demand," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There was some dollar buying by the Reserve Bank of India at 35.82 and later in the afternoon, a large state-run bank also came in to buy dollars."
This pushed the rupee down to its closing levels, he said.
Dealers said the rupee weakened against the forward dollar on paying pressure.
"A number of banks which had built up receiving positions seemed to have unwound these today," said a dealer. "This put some pressure on forward premia which moved up slightly."
The annualised premia on six-month dollars ended Tuesday at 7.71 percent from Monday's close of 7.54 percent, dealers said.
